headline: On November 1, 1987: British Rail Class 43 (HST) sets speed record
captionCards: This record highlighted the advancement in rail tech
instagramCaption:
British Rail Class 43 (HST) breaks speed records.
On November 1, 1987, the British Rail Class 43 (HST) achieved a top speed of 238 km/h. This diesel-electric train, built by British Rail Engineering Limited from 1975 to 1982, set the record for rail vehicles with on-board fuel. The HST, known as the InterCity 125, has been in service in the UK since 1976. This achievement showcased the engineering prowess and reliability of British trains. Why is this still relevant? It marked a significant milestone in railway technology.
